Hunting, weapons and animals

Hunting is the renewable food in survival. No animal fights back, so the only hard part is getting close enough and keeping the weapon ready.

Voxelgame main dd29d91 · 4 min read · Everyone · feature ledger · all guides

  2. Hit with a hand, tool or sword

Animals are passive

Every animal is passive. None of them attack, chase or damage you. Farm animals stay calm near you. Wild animals keep their distance and run when you come close. Peaceful world: no hostile mobs Animal behaviour

Good to know. There is no taming, riding, breeding, feeding, milking or shearing.

Hit with a hand, tool or sword

  1. Get within reach of the animal and aim at it.
  2. Left-click to hit it.
  3. A hurt animal runs off for a few seconds. Chase it and hit it again.

A bare hand or an ordinary tool deals 12 damage. The Stone sword deals 28. In creative, one hit removes the animal and gives you nothing. Tall grass or flowers between you and the animal can block the hit. Hitting animals (melee)

Crafted tools are equipped automatically.

Throwing rocks

Key or actionWhat it does
Hold right clickWind up. A full wind-up takes 0.7 s.
Release right clickThrow. A wind-up that is too short is cancelled.

Harder throws fly farther and hit harder. Each throw uses one rock in survival. Rocks hurt animals only, not you or vehicles. Throwing rocks

Tools & arms 1 recipes
RecipeMakesNeeds
Four throwing rocks4× Throwing rock
  • 4× Natural stone (any of 26 natural stones; mixable)

Each Throwing rock weighs 0.6 kg versus 0.125 kg per stone piece, so crafting rocks raises carried mass.

Alder bow and arrows

  1. Craft an Alder bow and some arrows.
  2. Equip the bow. Press Tab or Shift + Tab to cycle through what you carry.
  3. Hold right click to draw. A full draw takes 0.85 s.
  4. Release to shoot. Letting go before about a fifth of a draw cancels the shot.
Key or actionWhat it does
Hold right click, releaseDraw and shoot.
Hold ShiftSneak to steady your aim.

Longer draws fly faster and hit harder. In survival each shot uses one arrow, and arrows are not recovered. Arrows stop on grass, flowers and other small plants. Creative arrows are unlimited. Alder bow and arrows

Alder rifle

Key or actionWhat it does
Left clickFire.
Hold right clickRaise the sights for less spread and sway. You cannot aim while it reloads.
Hold ShiftSneak to steady your aim.
RDoes not reload the rifle. In survival, R eats food instead.

The rifle reloads itself about one second after every shot. Survival uses one rifle round per shot; creative is unlimited. Rounds hurt animals, characters and vehicles. Alder rifle and rifle rounds

Tools & arms 2 recipes
RecipeMakesNeeds
Alder rifle1× Alder rifle
  • 40× Natural stone (any of 26 natural stones; mixable)
  • 16× Boards of any species (Alder, Birch or Pine boards; mixable)
  • 8× Lumen crystal

40 stone = 5 blocks, 16 boards = 2 blocks, 8 Lumen crystal = 1 block. Needs Lumen crystal, which does not generate naturally: the only piece in a survival world sits at the Stone overlook landmark, so this recipe cannot be completed from gathered materials alone.

Four rifle rounds4× Rifle round
  • 8× Natural stone (any of 26 natural stones; mixable)
  • 8× Pale sand
  • 8× Lumen crystal

Needs Lumen crystal, which does not generate naturally: the only piece in a survival world sits at the Stone overlook landmark, so this recipe cannot be completed from gathered materials alone.

What you get from a kill

In survival, drops go straight into your pack. Meat and venison are food, feathers make arrows, and wool can replace plant fiber. Hide has no use yet. If your pack is full, drops that do not fit are lost, because there are no items on the ground. Creative kills give nothing. Animal drops

  • 4× Boards of any species (Alder, Birch or Pine boards; mixable)
Cook raw meat1× Cooked meat
  • 1× Raw meat
  • 1× Charcoal

Raw meat restores 8 hunger, Cooked meat 30.

Roast venison2× Cooked meat
  • 1× Venison
  • 1× Charcoal

One Venison (18 hunger raw) becomes 2 Cooked meat (30 each).

Cook meat over charcoal before you eat it. Cooked meat restores much more hunger than raw meat. See Your first survival day for the hunger numbers.
